exercise.name: Stair Climber
library_steps: Step on and start at a slow, steady speed.
Climb with your whole foot on each step, standing tall off the rails.
Slow it down and wait for the steps to stop before stepping off.
exercise.one_line_summary: Climbing revolving stairs, upright, hands off the rails. Picture 1: left foot on the higher step (knee bent ~75 deg), right on the lower one; picture 2: the other way round. Arms swing opposite to the legs.

setup.target: Upright, whole foot on each step.

muscles.emg: Knee extensors do most of the work to lift the body (S1).
muscles.role: Library primary 'cardio' has no mask; front thigh lit (library secondary).

muscles.emg: Plantarflexors push off the trailing foot (S1).

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Body weight held by the arms.
mistakes.why_it_matters: Takes the work off the legs (S1).

sources.citation: Nadeau S, McFadyen BJ, Malouin F. Frontal and sagittal plane analyses of the stair climbing task in healthy adults aged over 40 years: what are the challenges compared to level walking? Clin Biomech. 2003;18(10):950-959.
sources.what_it_gave: Stair climbing: knee extensors produce most of the work to lift the body onto the step; hip extensors and plantarflexors help.

clip_check.check: Machine parts meet the hands/feet; levers keep their length
clip_check.target: moving rod lengths equal at start and end (+-1 cm)
